Open to AI leadership roles in Germany

I build generative AI for machines that cannot be allowed to fail.

Turbines, compressors, rotating equipment. The data is sensor time-series and forty years of engineering documents, and being wrong has physical consequences.

I am a Lead AI/ML Engineer at Siemens Energy with 11+ years in production software and machine learning. For the last four I have been building and operating generative AI systems for industrial turbomachinery — not demos, but services that engineering and field teams depend on daily across three international sites.

The gap I work in

Plenty of people can build a RAG chatbot. Plenty understand rotating equipment. The overlap is close to empty.

Most AI engineers come from fintech, e-commerce or SaaS, where a wrong answer costs a refund. I come from assets worth tens of millions of euros, where a missed anomaly costs an unplanned outage and a hallucinated torque value is a safety problem.

That changes the engineering. Retrieval has to survive scanned P&IDs from the 1980s and datasheets whose meaning lives in table structure. Evaluation has to answer "is this grounded?" rather than "does this sound helpful?". Deployment has to sit inside enterprise data-protection, access-control and audit requirements. Everything on this site comes out of doing that work in production.

Selected work

Three systems

Production RAG over engineering documentation

Retrieval-augmented platform over technical manuals and industrial sensor data, using Azure OpenAI and Model Context Protocol. Lookups that took 20–30 minutes now return in under a minute.

  • MCP

Real-time anomaly detection for gas turbines

Event-driven pipeline on Step Functions, EventBridge, Lambda and SageMaker with automated alerting, replacing manual condition-monitoring rounds.

  • AWS
  • Time-series
  • XGBoost
  • Event-driven

An LLMOps practice, built from nothing

Prompt and model versioning, MLflow registry, a golden evaluation set gating every release, drift and cost monitoring on a dashboard the team actually reads.
